All steps in a wave complete together; newly released dependents may enter only the next wave. Repeat until all steps finish. Return {"ok":1,"waves":[[id,...],...]}, including no empty waves. Example: {"tasks":[8,3],"edges":[[8,3]],"capacity":2} gives {"ok":1,"waves":[[8],[3]]}. Read one JSON value from stdin and print one JSON value plus a newline, with no other stdout. Only integer numeric syntax is accepted (no floats or exponents); reject booleans, nulls, strings where integers are required, duplicate object keys, and trailing data. On invalid input print exactly {"ok":0} and exit zero. Reject missing or extra object fields, wrong shapes, and all bounds violations. Implement with Python's standard library; the starter contains parsing and shape validation, but the core operation is unfinished. Only the named entry file may be edited.
